design_detail: Editorial notice, not a study: the expression of concern about Ponte et al. (2021, Journal of Traumatic Stress 34:851-863), issued by agreement between the journal's Editor-in-Chief (Denise Sloan), the International Society for Traumatic Stress Studies and Wiley; published online 3 December 2024, Journal of Traumatic Stress 38(3), p. 555 (print issue June 2025 per Crossref). One short notice of four paragraphs; no authors are listed (Crossref has none). Card design 'narrative-review' is the schema's closest category for an editorial notice, as for the 2024 retraction notes (sc_jerome_2024). Reference id assigned by this reader (journal abbreviation and print year, since there is no author); the editor may prefer another.
can_establish: That the journal placed an expression of concern on the pooled sleep analysis, the reasons and the timeline it gives, and that the data of four MP-4 participants were to be removed by correction.
cannot_establish: What the ethical violation was, how it affected the data, or whether the analysis's conclusions hold: the notice gives none of this, and it says the journal's investigation of the human-subjects ethics questions was inconclusive.

analysis.selective_reporting: The notice does not describe the violation, does not quantify how much of the analysed data came from the two therapists beyond the four participants, and does not say what the IRB reports found in detail.

interpretation_gap.results_show: An editorial decision: the authors asked in early 2024 to remove four MP-4 participants treated by a pair of therapists involved in an ethical violation that caused a protocol deviation; the journal and Wiley investigated, agreed to a correction and issued the expression of concern because the authors' failure to report the violation at submission was judged improper, while the investigation of human-subjects ethics was inconclusive.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The notice claims nothing beyond its grounds; it states that all authors agree with it.

timeline.event: October 2018: report from Chesapeake IRB (now Advarra) to MAPS Public Benefit Corporation (now Lykos Therapeutics) on the ethical violation, as the notice reports.
May 2019: the violation is publicly announced; December 2019: the article is submitted without notifying the journal (per the notice).
March 2022: Advarra's follow-up report finds that the deviation and violation occurred during the trial as well as during the long-term follow-up (per the notice).

Early 2024: the authors contact the journal (per the notice). 10 August 2024: Psychopharmacology retracts three other phase 2 analyses of the same sponsor; Jerome, Mithoefer and Feduccia, authors of this article, are authors of all three (author lists in the Crossref records of the retraction notes feduccia_2024, jerome_2024 and mithoefer_2024).
3 December 2024: this expression of concern and the correction (jts_2025b) are published.

replication.where_it_stands: In force. The article is not retracted and may be cited, with the notice, for its corrected figures (sc_jts_2025b); the notice itself may be cited for the journal's decision and the timeline it states.

funding.declared_conflicts: Not applicable. The notice states that MAPS Public Benefit Corporation (now Lykos Therapeutics) received the IRB reports and finalized a clinical study report before the authors contacted the journal.
funding.affiliations_note: The two therapists involved were not co-authors of the article (per the notice).

what_would_settle_it: Publication of the IRB findings and of the sponsor's clinical study report for MP-4, and an independent reanalysis of the pooled phase 2 data with the affected site's data handled transparently.

domains.note: Not a review: the notice reports the journal's own decision on one article.
The notice relies on reports the authors shared and does not describe the violation or its effect on the data.

domains.domain: Reliance on the authors' own studies
domains.note: Concerns only the article it qualifies.
States the decision, its grounds and the dates without speculation.

domains.domain: Balance of the parties' accounts (the authors' account at submission and the IRB's later findings are both given)
domains.note: The notice gives the authors' account at submission (violation thought to have occurred after treatment) and the March 2022 finding that it occurred during the trial as well.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: No validated instrument applies to an editorial notice; the editors' narrative-review checklist is used, its domains read as questions about the notice as a source. It is the primary record of the expression of concern and may be cited for the decision, its grounds and its dates; it gives no account of the violation itself.

key_findings.finding: Expression of concern for Ponte et al. (2021), issued by agreement between the Editor-in-Chief, the International Society for Traumatic Stress Studies and Wiley; published 3 December 2024 (Journal of Traumatic Stress 38(3):555).
key_findings.locator: Notice header; 2nd paragraph (the first after the citation of the article)

key_findings.finding: The authors asked the journal to remove the data of 4 participants of the MP-4 study (NCT01958593, October 2014 to October 2016), in which an ethical violation by a pair of therapists, who treated 4 of the 6 MP-4 participants included, caused a deviation from the protocol; neither therapist was a co-author.

Timeline given by the notice: a report from Chesapeake IRB (now Advarra) to MAPS Public Benefit Corporation (now Lykos Therapeutics) in October 2018; public announcement of the violation in May 2019; submission of the article in December 2019 without notifying the journal, the violation being described at the time as having occurred after treatment, during long-term follow-up, and all participants being included under the intention-to-treat principle; Advarra's March 2022 follow-up report found that it had occurred during the trial as well; the authors contacted the journal in early 2024, after a compliance review by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of British Columbia and the finalization of the sponsor's clinical study report.

Decision: all data provided by the two therapists are removed by correction (10.1002/jts.23098); the expression of concern is issued because the authors' conduct in not initially reporting the violation was judged improper, while the investigation into violations of Wiley's and the journal's ethical guidelines on human-subjects research proved inconclusive; all authors agree with the notice.

reporting_issues.issue: The notice refers to the 4 MP-4 participants as 4 of 6 'included in the MP-4 study', while the correction says 4 of 6 MP-4 participants 'out of the 68 participants included in the pooled analysis'; the article's pooled sample was 63.
reporting_issues.page: PMC HTML (Notice, 2nd paragraph); correction, Description and explanation
reporting_issues.consequence: The denominator of 68 in the correction is unexplained (see sc_jts_2025b).

verification.source_read: PMC full text PMC12416979 (the whole notice), read with the article (PMC8453707) and the correction (publisher HTML, free access). Crossref record read in this reader's tab: no authors; update-to link to 10.1002/jts.22696 of type expression_of_concern.
